Transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is a scoping call to make sure the poc covers the latency and throughput targets you care about. maya, do you want to quickly frame success criteria from saintlane?
[00:15] Maya (SaintLane): yeah thanks avery. main thing for us is responsiveness in our user-facing assistant — low first reply time and consistent token throughput. we have two distinct flows: short queries (5-40 tokens) and long summary generation (200-800 tokens). the first is very latency sensitive.
[00:35] Priya (SaintLane CTO): also cost matters — we cant blow up our infra budget. but reliability and p99 behavior is biggest for legal/regulatory user sessions.
[00:48] Diego (Redwood SE): cool. so we'll scope both TTFT — time to first token — and TPOT — time per output token / throughput. we typically measure p95 and p99 for both. quick note: sometimes transcripts write TPOT differently, you'll see a few mixes in our docs.
[01:10] Jordan (SaintLane): can you define the exact metrics you'll report? we need them to match our SLO format in SRE.
[01:22] Diego (Redwood SE): yes. for TTFT we'll report median, p95, p99. TTFT is measured from request received by the front end of the runtime to first byte of model output. for TPOT we measure per-token latency: tokens/sec or ms/token, aggregated to give p50/p95/p99. we'll also give overall end-to-end latency for full-response flows, and 95/99 for cold starts.
[01:45] Maya (SaintLane): what are realistic targets?
[01:50] Avery (Redwood AE): from our experience with similar customers, hosteds defaults: TTFT p95 around 120-250ms for short prompts on optimized models, p99 around 300-600ms depending on region and concurrency. TPOT p95 can be ~15-35ms per token for streaming scenarios. Dedicated GPU pools get you lower variance — p99 closer to 250-400ms TTFT for short prompts.
[02:15] Priya (SaintLane CTO): that's a bit wide. can you propose concrete targets we can commit to for the POC?
[02:22] Diego (Redwood SE): propose we use two target tiers for the POC:
- Tier A (interactive): TTFT p95 <= 200ms, TTFT p99 <= 400ms for 5-40 token prompts; TPOT p95 <= 25ms/token.
- Tier B (batch/long): Full-response end-to-end p95 <= 2.5s for 200 token outputs (equiv. ~12.5ms/token average), p99 <= 4s.
these are achievable on Dedicated with right batch config and kv-cache priming; Hosted can meet Tier A for many models but depends on region and noisy neighbors.
[03:05] Maya (SaintLane): sounds reasonable, we like explicit p99 numbers. can you also capture tail behaviors at high concurrency? we saw bad p99 spikes in our current in-house endpoint at ~120 concurrent sessions.
[03:20] Diego (Redwood SE): absolutely. measurement plan should include a stress sweep across concurrency: 10, 30, 60, 120, 240 concurrent requests; measure p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT at each point. also record CPU/GPU utilization, memory, and queue lengths.
[03:42] Jordan (SaintLane): what's your recommended QPS and sequence lengths for the sweep?
[03:47] Avery (Redwood AE): we'll use three workload profiles you provided: interactive short (avg 20 tokens, bursts up to 150 QPS), conversational medium (avg 120 tokens, steady 40 QPS), and long summarization (avg 350 tokens, 5-10 QPS). please confirm those numbers on uploading prompts.
[04:10] Maya (SaintLane): yes that matches our telemetry, interactive is busiest. we'll upload 2,000 real prompts and a synthetic generator.
[04:22] Diego (Redwood SE): good. test harness: we'll run Locust + custom payload runner, and also run our internal bench tool to measure TTFT at 1ms resolution. we'll provide the test config so your SREs can reproduce. link to bench sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/saintlane-poc (note: placeholder link in transcript).
[04:45] Priya (SaintLane CTO): what about caching? our app has a lot of repeated prefixes and a warm KV cache helped previously. how do you measure that effect?
[04:54] Diego (Redwood SE): we'll do two passes: cold (empty KV) and warm (prime KV with 20k common prefixes). measure delta on TTFT and TPOT at p95/p99. we expect warm cache to reduce TTFT by 30-60% for repeated flows.
[05:18] Maya (SaintLane): quantization and model variant choices — we have constraints on output quality. we cant use aggressive quant if it changes hallucination rates.
[05:26] Diego (Redwood SE): understood. for the POC we'll compare three model variants: FP16 baseline, int8 quant (LLM.int8), and a tuned int8+kv profile. we'll run automated evals on a held-out prompt set for quality regressions and surf report (we'll push the eval results as separate artifact).
[05:52] Avery (Redwood AE): from a contracting perspective, are you considering Hosted POC or Dedicated reserved capacity?
[05:59] Priya (SaintLane CTO): we'd like to test Hosted first because it's fastest to stand up, but if the p99 tail or cost is bad, we'll move to Dedicated. POC should include both comparisons if possible.
[06:12] Diego (Redwood SE): that's straightforward. we'll run the identical bench converstions on Redwood Hosted region (us-west) and a Dedicated pool with 4xA100-equivalent GPUs. note: dedicated config may require a short provisioning window.
[06:30] Jordan (SaintLane): how long will the POC benchmarking take and what's the timeline for results?
[06:35] Avery (Redwood AE): propose timeline: week 0 (2026-12-14 to 12-18): collect prompts & traffic profiles; week 1 (2026-12-21 to 12-25): bench runs + initial compare; week 2 (2026-12-28 to 01-01): tuning runs (batching/quant/kv configs) and quality evals; week 3 (2027-01-04): present final results and recommendations. we can compress if needed but need at least one full warm/cold cycle.
[07:05] Priya (SaintLane CTO): we have year-end freezes — can we aim for the week of 2026-12-21 for the first runs?
[07:12] Avery (Redwood AE): yes we'll aim for that.
[07:16] Maya (SaintLane): measurement details — what's the exact definition of cold start? we had different meanings internally.
[07:22] Diego (Redwood SE): we'll define cold as a request after a 10-minute idle period for that model shard, where KV cache is empty and the model process may be spun down. warm is steady traffic. we'll also record instance startup times separately (bootstrap latency).
[07:40] Jordan (SaintLane): do you measure network delays separately? our infra sits behind a CDN and there's some edge time to consider.
[07:47] Diego (Redwood SE): yes we'll report both client-to-runtime (observed at client agent) and runtime internal (service ingress to first token) so you can subtract network tail. we can instrument with tcpdump traces or monitoring to isolate.
[08:05] Maya (SaintLane): what about SLO alerting thresholds? for example we only want pages on p99 > 500ms for interactive flows.
[08:12] Avery (Redwood AE): recommend SLOs for production: p95 <= 180ms and p99 <= 350ms for interactive; page / pager if p99 > 500ms sustained for 5 minutes. for batch/long jobs use percent error budgets on throughput. but POC targets as diego suggested earlier.
[08:36] Diego (Redwood SE): another important metric is variance under load: the coefficient of variation for TPOT across the run. we'll capture 1min windows to show instability.
[08:50] Maya (SaintLane): will you include cost estimates per 1M tokens for each mode?
[08:56] Avery (Redwood AE): yes, we'll include unit economics: cost per 1M tokens for Hosted vs Dedicated assumptions with projected savings from batching/caching. we'll call out tradeoffs.
[09:08] Priya (SaintLane CTO): security/reg compliance: we need SOC2 + KMS encryption keys for dedicated. how does that affect benching?
[09:16] Diego (Redwood SE): encryption kos doesn't change model perf significantly, but network encryption and KMS HSM calls add a small overhead on cold starts. we'll measure with KMS enabled for Dedicated runs. also will provide our security pack.
[09:36] Jordan (SaintLane): any limitations around sequence length and attention that's important? our summarization sometimes goes 1200 tokens.
[09:43] Diego (Redwood SE): we asked you to trim to 800 for bench to keep runs comparable; for production we can support 1200 but cost and per-token latency goes up quadratically in some parts of the stack. we'll run a few long-tail tests at 1200 too.
[10:00] Maya (SaintLane): any gotchas you recommend for the benchmark harness?
[10:04] Diego (Redwood SE): randomization of prompts, ensure sticky sessions for conversational flows to keep KV hit realistic, ramp-up to steady state for 5 minutes at each concurrency level, and collect hardware counters. avoid synthetic super-short inter-request pauses, emulate client jitter. we'll share configs.
[10:28] Avery (Redwood AE): ok let's capture the POC success criteria succinctly so everyone is clear.
[10:33] Maya (SaintLane): yes
[10:35] Diego (Redwood SE): POC success criteria (proposed):
- Metric targets: Tier A: TTFT p95 <= 200ms, TTFT p99 <= 400ms (5-40 token interactive); TPOT p95 <= 25ms/token.
- Tier B: full-response (200-400 tokens) p95 <= 2.5s, p99 <= 4s.
- Stability: no p99 spikes > 2x baseline under expected concurrency for >5 minutes.
- Quality: no measurable degradation on held-out eval (<= 1% metric delta on rouge/embedding-sim).
- Cost: expected cost per 1M tokens below threshold (we'll put exact numbers in spreadsheet).
[11:05] Priya (SaintLane CTO): that list looks good. please add a clause about security/compliance checklist completion as a gating item for Dedicated.
[11:12] Avery (Redwood AE): will do.
[11:15] Maya (SaintLane): for reporting format, can you provide CSVs with p50/p95/p99 by concurrency and a dashboard link?
[11:22] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, we'll provide raw logs, aggregated CSVs, and a Grafana-like dashboard snapshot.
[11:30] Jordan (SaintLane): who will own running the benchmark? will Redwood run them or do we run in our environment?
[11:36] Avery (Redwood AE): Redwood can run both sides; ideally we run them jointly — Redwood kicks off load from our test agents and your infra runs a receive endpoint. if you want to run them entirely in your env we'll share the harness and configs.
[11:50] Maya (SaintLane): ok great. last: any recommended fallback policies if we see p99 breaches in production?
[11:56] Diego (Redwood SE): we recommend auto-fallback to smaller model shard or lower-precision variant for degraded latency, with canary checks to ensure quality isn't catastrophically impacted. Redwood runtime supports policy-based routing and auto-failover — we'll demo that in the follow-up.
[12:18] Avery (Redwood AE): awesome. to recap next steps: avery to send pricing and bench sheet, diego to prepare load config and run plan, maya to upload prompts and profiles, schedule bench run week of 12/21.
[12:30] Priya (SaintLane CTO): thanks everyone.
[12:32] Maya (SaintLane): thank you.
[12:34] Diego (Redwood SE): thanks all. followups in email.
